thread:
Sofia (CSM): Heads-up — onboarding for HelixHealth just spiked. They started a large embedding run yesterday and credits are burning faster than forecasted. Can we preemptively allocate and avoid a renewal friction issue?

Arjun (FinOps): I saw that. Forecaster shows a 3x spike vs baseline if they continue. They have auto-billing on but we should still flag before it hits their budget alert.

Maya (Enablement): Do we know what part of the flow triggered it? Is it embeddings, fine-tuning, or heavy sampling?

Sofia (CSM): It's embeddings + frequent similarity queries for their search index rebuild. Eli said they kicked off a reindex after ingesting a month of events.

Eli (Customer): yep — we reindexed yesterday to include yesterday's batch. We can throttle but need guidance on cost-friendly settings.

Arjun (FinOps): Quick options: 1) cap qps on their route, 2) enable prefix caching for repeated queries, 3) allocate a short-term credits top-up, or 4) switch embeddings to a slightly lower-cost quantized model for the rebuild window.

Priya (Solutions): I can run a model-swap experiment. For the reindex window we can route requests to emb-lite-quant and measure quality delta. If quality OK, we keep it for 48h.

Maya (Enablement): Also recommend a short playbook for Eli: add batching, set max_tokens per call, and use deterministic sampling off. Small changes multiply at scale.

Sofia (CSM): Action list: Priya to test emb-lite-quant + report by 2pm PT. Arjun to propose a one-time credits allocation and set budget alert thresholds. Maya to send a quick enablement snippet for Eli. I'll follow up in QBR prep doc. :thumbsup:

Arjun (FinOps): Proposed temporary credit allocation: 20% of their monthly commit or 10k credits (whichever smaller) with a hard cap. Approve?

Eli (Customer): 10k credits sounds fine for a 48h window. Please also set an automated alert at 60% usage so our infra team can throttle if needed.

Priya (Solutions): Running local quality check now. If it passes, I'll post an eval sample.

ops-bot: Budget alert created for HelixHealth — threshold: 60% of allocation. Notification will post in #customer-billing and DM @Eli.

Arjun (FinOps): Config I'm going to push (example):
```
budget_alerts: 
  - account: helixhealth
    window: 48h
    allocation: 10000
    notify_channels: ["customer-billing", "cs-sofia"]
    hard_cap: true
```

Maya (Enablement): Short snippet for Eli: 
- Use batch_size=64 for embed calls
- Prefer incremental reindex (30m chunks) vs full run
- Switch sampling to deterministic where possible

Sofia (CSM): For the QBR, we'll include this as a 'cost-surge mitigation' example and add recommended runbook steps. Also capture feedback: Eli to send a 1-paragraph note on whether emb-lite quality was acceptable.

Eli (Customer): Will do. Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage.

Priya (Solutions): Update: emb-lite quality sample looks 92% similar on our automated metric. Sending samples in 10m.

Arjun (FinOps): Pushed the allocation. ops-bot confirmed. I'll also add a line-item in the QBR forecast slide: "Emergency buffer used: 10k credits — impact on runway: -3 days" so renewals team sees it.

Sofia (CSM): Perfect. I'll draft the QBR note and capture actions + feedback. Closing here once Priya posts samples and Eli confirms alert behavior.

Eli (Customer): Alert arrived as expected. No surprises so far.

Priya (Solutions): Samples posted in thread. Quality tradeoff acceptable for reindex.

Sofia (CSM): Thanks — closing loop. I'll attach this thread to the QBR doc and tag the renewal owner. :white_check_mark:
